description: This is a modern 'Namespaces View' dashboard for your Kubernetes cluster(s). Made for kube-prometheus-stack and take advantage of the latest Grafana features. GitHub repository: https://github.com/dotdc/grafana-dashboards-kubernetes Adapted from dotdc/grafana-dashboards-kubernetes (Apache-2.0, https://github.com/dotdc/grafana-dashboards-kubernetes); modified. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

links.title: Fleet overview
links.tooltip: The home page: is anything wrong, and where?

links.title: Kubernetes views
links.tooltip: Cluster, namespace and pod drill-down views

panels.title: Namespace(s) usage on total cluster CPU in %
panels.description: Share of the whole cluster's CPU the selected namespaces use. High means these namespaces dominate: check their requests against usage.

panels.title: Namespace(s) usage on total cluster RAM in %
panels.description: Share of the whole cluster's memory the selected namespaces use. High means these namespaces dominate the cluster.

panels.title: Kubernetes Resource Count
panels.description: How many of each Kubernetes object the cluster holds. Use it to spot a runaway controller creating objects without bound.

targets.expr: sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace", resource="cpu", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"} and on(namespace, pod) max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Running", namespace=~"$namespace", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"} == 1))

sum(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace=~"$namespace", resource="cpu", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"} and on(namespace, pod) max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Running", namespace=~"$namespace", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"} == 1))

panels.title: Namespace(s) CPU Usage in cores
panels.description: CPU cores the selected namespaces use right now.

targets.expr: sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace", resource="memory", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"} and on(namespace, pod) max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Running", namespace=~"$namespace", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"} == 1))

sum(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace=~"$namespace", resource="memory", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"} and on(namespace, pod) max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Running", namespace=~"$namespace", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"} == 1))

panels.title: Namespace(s) RAM Usage in bytes
panels.description: Working-set memory the selected namespaces use right now.

panels.title: CPU usage by Pod
panels.description: CPU cores used per pod in the selected namespaces. Click a series to open the pod, and compare with its requests and limits there.

panels.title: Memory usage by Pod
panels.description: Working-set memory per pod in the selected namespaces. A climbing line is a leak; click a series to open the pod.
Seconds per second a pod was held back by its CPU limit. Above zero: raise the limit, or drop it for latency-sensitive work.
panels.title: CPU Throttled seconds by pod
Kubernetes Pods QoS classes
panels.description: Pods by quality-of-service class. Many BestEffort pods are the first evicted under pressure: give them requests.

panels.title: Kubernetes Pods Status Reason
panels.description: Pods whose status carries a reason (for example Evicted or NodeLost). Anything here is a pod the cluster gave up on: find the reason and its node.
No data is generally a good thing here.
panels.title: OOM Events by namespace, pod

panels.description: No data is generally a good thing here.
panels.title: Container Restarts by namespace, pod
Nb of pods by state
panels.description: Containers by readiness. Not ready for long means a failing probe or a crash: open the pod.

panels.title: Nb of containers by pod
panels.description: Container count per pod. A sudden change is a rollout or a sidecar added or lost.

panels.title: Replicas available by deployment
panels.description: Available replicas per Deployment. Below the desired count means a rollout is stuck or pods cannot start.

panels.title: Replicas unavailable by deployment
panels.description: Unavailable replicas per Deployment. Above zero for long means pods are not starting: open the namespace's failing pods.
List of pods that are not in Running or Succeeded status.
panels.title: Pods with unexpected status
Container Image Used
panels.description: Which container images the selected pods run. Use it to confirm a rollout reached every pod.

targets.expr: max(kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}) by (persistentvolumeclaim, namespace) / max(kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", k8s_cluster_name="$cluster"}) by (persistentvolumeclaim, namespace)

panels.title: Persistent Volumes - Capacity and usage in %
panels.description: Used space as a share of each volume's capacity. Above 85% expand the claim or clean up before it fills.

panels.title: Persistent Volumes - Capacity and usage in bytes
panels.description: Used and total bytes per volume. Read the growth rate to estimate when it fills.

panels.title: Persistent Volumes - Inodes
panels.description: Used inodes as a share of capacity per volume. Running out of inodes stops writes even with free space: clean up small files.

panels.title: Network - Bandwidth by pod
panels.description: Bytes per second received and sent per pod. A pod far above its peers is the noisy one.

panels.title: Network - Packets Rate by pod
panels.description: Packets per second received and sent per pod. Use it beside bandwidth to tell many small packets from few large ones.

panels.title: Network - Packets Dropped by pod
panels.description: Packets dropped per second per pod. Above zero means saturation or a broken network policy: check the node and the CNI.

panels.title: Network - Errors by pod
panels.description: Network errors per second per pod. Above zero points at a faulty interface or CNI: check the node.

list.description: Can be used to filter on a specific deployment, statefulset or deamonset (only relevant panels).
